4.1.1 Flora
The Applicant arranged for a botanical survey of the project area by Dr. C. Leland Rodgers and J.E. Green, Jr., of Furman University. The surveyors identified three major communities: hardwoods on slopes, hardwoods on ravines and valleys, and pines on ridges and shallow soil. The results of this 1973 survey are contained in Appendix D of the Applicant's Exhibit W.
Mr. R. A. Cloninger, Forester for the Applicant, also conducted a forest tree survey of the project area in May 1973. He determined that the area was covered with an oakhickory forest type, win some shortleaf pine occurring at lower elevations and white pine and eastern hemlock growing in the upper mountain regions. This survey is contained in Appendix E of the Applicant's Exhibit W.
Dr. Rodger's survey (Section 4.1.1) of the vegetation of the project area included four plant species identified as rare or rare in the geographical area (Section 2.2.3.1). The survey recommended that some plants of ginseng, American climbing fern, and wintergreen be relocated to similar nearby habitants. The Fraser's lysimachia is considered to be abundant and hearty in adjacent areas, so transplanting specimens would not be warranted.
Under the direction of Dr. Rodgers, specimens of ginseng, American climbing fern, wintergreen, witch alder, and lysimachia have been transplanted to areas outside the project. Table 4.2 shows the number of specimens transplanted. Applicant reports that observations made in May 1975 showed the transplants to be thriving.
